contextual.summary: If your home postcode is in the most deprived IMD group (IMD deciles 1 and 2, which Liverpool calls Quintile 1) or you have spent any time in care, Liverpool automatically gives you a reduced offer of up to two grades below the standard offer.
contextual.typicalReduction: Up to two grades below the standard offer (exceptions may apply; not Medicine, Dental Sciences or Foundation programmes)

criteria.detail: Home postcode on your UCAS application is in IMD Decile 1 or 2 (Liverpool's 'Quintile 1', the most deprived group). The scheme is for UK students; the postcode is checked automatically.
Care experienced: you have spent any amount of time in Local Authority care before your 18th birthday and meet the nationally used eligibility criteria (UK students).

contextual.rulesText: Reduced offers are automatic (no extra form): you get an offer of up to two grades below the standard offer if your postcode is in IMD Quintile 1 or you have spent any time in social care. Where a range is used, the standard offer is the upper grade profile. If you qualify for a reduction for more than one reason, it stays at a maximum of two grades. Other contextual indicators (for example disability, disrupted studies, UCAS MEM data) are used for additional consideration, such as at interview or on results day, not for an automatic reduced offer.

source.evidence: up to a 2-grade reduction* from the standard offer ... Index of Multiple Deprivation (IMD) Deciles 1 and 2 ... UK Care Experienced students

programmes.name: Pathways to Banking and Finance
programmes.provider: University of Liverpool (with the Sutton Trust)
programmes.summary: Free 2-year project for Year 12 students from widening participation backgrounds, with taster sessions at Liverpool, banking and finance work experience, a 3-day residential at the University of Warwick and A-level tutoring in Year 13.
programmes.whoCanApply: Current Year 12 students who have always attended a state-funded, non-fee-paying school or college, have at least 5 GCSEs at grade 9-4 including Maths at grade 5, meet at least one widening participation criterion and can commute to the University of Liverpool.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Students must: have always attended a state-funded, non-fee-paying school or college; be a current Year 12 student; have at least 5 GCSEs at grade 9-4 including GCSE Maths at grade 5; be able to commute to the University of Liverpool. They should also meet at least one of: parents have not attended university; receiving or eligible for free school meals at secondary school; attend a school or college with a below-average A-level or Higher point score and/or a low rate of progression to higher education; live in a neighbourhood with a low rate of progression to higher education and/or high socio-economic deprivation; have been looked after or in care. Meeting more criteria makes a place more likely.
benefits: Free: travel, accommodation, food and activities are paid for by the Sutton Trust and the University of Liverpool
University taster sessions on campus and work experience placements in banking and finance
3-day residential conference at the University of Warwick
A-level tutoring in Year 13 and advice on UCAS and Student Finance
Further on-course support if you go on to study at Liverpool
programmes.subjects: Business-related degrees and careers in banking and finance (including Economics, Accounting and Finance, Business Management, Finance and Data Analytics)

programmes.name: Liverpool Scholars Programme
programmes.summary: Year 12 programme of application masterclasses, lectures and academic skills workshops; completing it gives a guaranteed conditional offer from Liverpool and an offer reduced by up to 2 A level grades.
programmes.whoCanApply: Year 12 students at Widening Participation and Outreach partner schools or colleges in Greater Merseyside who are Home (UK) students and meet at least two of the listed widening participation criteria (or one of the alternative criteria).
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Step 1 (all of): study at one of the Widening Participation and Outreach partner schools or colleges in Greater Merseyside; ideally at least five GCSEs at grade 9-6 (grade 4 or above in English Language and Maths if these are not among them); be a Home (UK) registered student or expect to be by the time you apply for higher education. Step 2 (at least two of): live in a neighbourhood with a low progression rate to higher education or high deprivation (POLAR4 quintile 1-2, or the 40% most deprived IMD wards); neither parent attended university; receive or be entitled to discretionary payments, a 16-19 bursary or Pupil Premium; receive or be entitled to free school meals (or have been in the last six years). Or alternatively: live or have lived in local authority care, be a young carer, or be estranged/living independently from your family; or have completed earlier Widening Participation and Outreach programmes (e.g. Merseyside Young Medics, Fast-trackers). Applications not meeting the criteria cannot normally be considered.
benefits: A guaranteed conditional offer of a place at the University of Liverpool (not necessarily your first-choice course)
An offer reduced by up to 2 A level grades or equivalent
Application guidance masterclasses, lectures and academic key skills workshops
